results.content:
Confirm it is ticking by watching the process output:

```
[AutonomyReconciler] Cron run complete — 1 projects, 0 fixes applied, 0 frozen 
```

`0 projects` is normal on a new install, and does not mean it is broken. A project is only reconciled once something has been built in it (a table other than the built-in `users` table, a function, a bucket, a trigger, a webhook or enabled auth) and it shows recent activity. A project that has only been named has nothing to be right or wrong about, so the loop skips it and files nothing against it. Create a table through your agent and the count becomes 1 on the next tick.

`CRON_SECRET` is not required for any of the above. It guards one ad-hoc endpoint, for forcing a tick without waiting for the minute: [...] > Restart your MCP host after installing. Tools stay absent until it reconnects, which looks like a broken install but is not one.

Verify the connection by asking your agent:

```
Call Backenly's read_backend_state tool and tell me what exists in this project. 
```

Then describe what you want. The SDK is for the app you ship:

```
const backend = new BackenlyClient({,}) await backend. auth. signUp({,}) await backend. posts. create({title 'Hello'}) await backend. posts. list({filter{published true}})
```

## Repository layout [...] Backenly does neither. You describe the product you're building through the coding agent you already use (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) over an MCP server. Backenly derives the data model, generates the endpoints, writes the policies, applies the change, and then verifies it against the live runtime. A continuous autonomy loop keeps watching after that, repairing drift, missing indexes, broken triggers, and RLS gaps on its own. When a table starts doing two jobs, Backenly moves the second into a table of its own once you approve, while your apps keep working, and every change can be undone from one History without rewinding your data.

results.content: AI coding agents can build an entire application in an afternoon. But building an application is only the beginning. What happens when the backend breaks after deployment? An API stops responding. The database schema gets out of sync. Permissions create security issues. A migration goes wrong. And suddenly, developers have to stop building new features and spend their time fixing backend problems. That's exactly the challenge Backenly is solving. Instead of making developers manually monitor and maintain everything, Backenly brings autonomous backend management directly into the AI coding workflow. Here's what makes it interesting: ➟ Database management: Create and manage Postgres databases with row-level security. ➟ Authentication: Handle user authentication without building everything [...] Handle user authentication without building everything from scratch. ➟ Storage & Realtime: Manage file storage, realtime updates, and backend functions in one place. ➟ Continuous monitoring: Backenly checks your running backend every minute to identify problems. ➟ Self-healing: It can fix issues it safely verifies, roll back when needed, and confirm whether the fix actually worked. ➟ Safer database changes: Rehearse database restructuring on a copy and propose changes before applying them to your live database. ➟ AI agent integration: Connect Backenly with Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex through MCP. But there's something important here. Autonomous doesn't mean giving AI complete control over your backend. Every change is reversible, verified, and recorded. Even destructive operations, like [...] verified, and recorded. Even destructive operations, like dropping a table, require your approval. What does this actually change? ✓ Spend less time monitoring backend issues. ✓ Let AI agents handle routine backend maintenance. ✓ Catch problems before they become bigger headaches. ✓ Make database changes with more confidence. ✓ Keep control over important and destructive operations. @shivam_kushwaha16Thanks Shivam, we actually take a checkpoint before every fix and verify the change right after. If verification fails, Backenly rolls back to that checkpoint automatically, but only if no rows written after the fix would be affected. If some would, the rollback waits for your approval and shows you exactly what it would change. You can also roll back any change yourself from History.
